transcript.text: This morning I confirmed with HR that, because this pilot follows repeated conduct concerns, it must meet four specific safeguard requirements: the peer-feedback pilot must be opt-in (not mandatory participation), it must use an independent neutral facilitator (not someone internal to the team), it must include a written non-retaliation acknowledgment that participants sign, and it must receive a documented review exactly 30 days after launch. These requirements were issued after the draft proposal had already circulated, so they haven't been incorporated into the current version of the proposal.

commitments.detail: Participation in the peer-feedback pilot will be strictly opt-in; no one will be required to participate.
An independent neutral facilitator external to the team will be engaged to run all facilitated sessions.
A written non-retaliation acknowledgment will be signed by each participant before participation.
A documented review of the pilot will be conducted exactly 30 days after launch.

An anonymous written channel will be offered as an alternative participation format within the opt-in structure, so colleagues who are not comfortable in the facilitated group setting can still contribute.

commitments.detail: The identities of the two colleagues who privately told Darius they would only contribute through an anonymous written channel will not be disclosed in the final plan or in any operational materials.
